title: Two Sum
description_html:
You are given an integer array nums and an integer target. Return the indices of the two numbers whose sum equals target.

Every input has exactly one valid answer, and the same element may not be used twice.

The two indices may be returned in any order.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,7,11,15], target = 9
Output: [0,1]
Explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, so the answer is [0, 1].

Example 2:

Input: nums = [3,2,4], target = 6
Output: [1,2]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [3,3], target = 6
Output: [0,1]

Constraints:

  • 2 <= nums.length <= 104
  • -109 <= nums[i] <= 109
  • -109 <= target <= 109
  • Exactly one valid answer exists.

Follow-up: Can you find an algorithm that runs in less than O(n2) time?
editorial_html:
Approach 1: Brute Force

Try every pair (i, j) with i < j and return the first pair whose values add up to target.

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: List[int], target: int) -> List[int]:
        for i in range(len(nums)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(nums)):
                if nums[i] + nums[j] == target:
                    return [i, j]
  • Time: O(n2) — every pair is examined in the worst case.
  • Space: O(1).

Approach 2: One-Pass Hash Map (Optimal)

Intuition. While scanning left to right, the only question for the current value x is "have I already seen target - x?". A hash map answers that in expected constant time.

Algorithm.

  1. Create an empty map seen from value to index.
  2. For each index i with value x:
    • If target - x is in seen, return [seen[target - x], i].
    • Otherwise record seen[x] = i.

Looking up the complement before inserting the current value guarantees an element is never paired with itself, and handles duplicates such as [3,3] naturally.

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: List[int], target: int) -> List[int]:
        seen = {}
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            if target - x in seen:
                return [seen[target - x], i]
            seen[x] = i
  • Time: O(n) — each element is visited once with O(1) expected map operations.
  • Space: O(n) for the map.
hints: A brute-force approach checks every pair of indices. What work is repeated across those checks?
For a value x, the partner you need is target - x. How quickly can you tell whether you have already seen it?
Keep a hash map from each value seen so far to its index, and look up the complement before inserting.
